helpModal.title: Encoder/Decoder User Manual
helpModal.overviewText: The Encoder/Decoder tool is a powerful multi-format conversion tool that supports Base64, Base64URL, URL, HTML, Hex, JWT, ROT13, ROT47, and Unicode encoding and decoding operations. This tool helps you quickly convert text formats, commonly used in data processing, web development, security analysis, and CTF challenges. Supports both text and file modes.
helpModal.base64Desc: A method of representing binary data using 64 printable characters, commonly used to transmit binary data in text protocols.
helpModal.base64urlDesc: URL-safe Base64 variant, removes +/= characters, used for JWT tokens and URL parameter passing.
helpModal.urlDesc: Converts special characters to URL-safe format, used for passing parameters and paths in URLs.
helpModal.htmlDesc: Converts HTML special characters to entity encoding, preventing XSS attacks and display issues.
helpModal.hexDesc: Converts text to hexadecimal representation, commonly used for low-level data analysis and debugging.
helpModal.jwtDesc: JSON Web Token decoder, parses JWT header, payload and signature.
helpModal.rot13Desc: Letter rotation by 13 positions, A↔N, B↔O, commonly used for simple text obfuscation and CTF challenges.
helpModal.rot47Desc: All printable ASCII characters rotation by 47 positions, stronger obfuscation than ROT13.
helpModal.unicodeDesc: Converts text to \uXXXX format, commonly used for XSS bypass and web security testing.
helpModal.step1: Select tool mode: Encode/Decode or Hash Calculation.
helpModal.step2: Select encoding type: Click the corresponding encoding type button.
helpModal.step3: Select operation: Encode, Decode, or Auto Detect.
helpModal.step4: Enter text: Input the text content to be processed in the left input box.
helpModal.step5: Process text: Click the 'Process' button, and the result will be displayed in the right output box.
helpModal.tip1: Use the 'Auto Detect' button to automatically identify the encoding type of input content.
helpModal.tip2: Use the 'Swap' button to quickly use the output result as new input and automatically switch encode/decode operation.
helpModal.tip3: Use the 'Copy' button to quickly copy the processing result to clipboard.
helpModal.tip4: JWT decoding supports automatic JSON formatting for easy viewing.
helpModal.tip5: ROT13 and ROT47 are self-inverse, encoding again equals decoding.

secHeaders.helpOverviewText: The HTTP Security Header Analyzer checks website security response header configuration, evaluates security grade, and provides improvement recommendations. Supports CSP detailed analysis, HSTS evaluation, cookie security check, and information leakage detection.
secHeaders.helpCsp: Controls which resources the browser can load, defends against XSS attacks
secHeaders.helpHsts: Forces browsers to use HTTPS connections, prevents protocol downgrade attacks
secHeaders.helpXfo: Prevents clickjacking attacks, controls iframe embedding
secHeaders.helpRp: Controls referrer information passing, prevents information leakage
secHeaders.helpPp: Controls browser feature permissions (camera, microphone, etc.)
secHeaders.helpCoop: Isolates cross-origin documents, defends against Spectre-style side-channel attacks
secHeaders.helpCorp: Controls cross-origin resource sharing, prevents cross-origin resource theft
secHeaders.helpCoep: Controls cross-origin embedder policy, enables advanced APIs like SharedArrayBuffer
secHeaders.helpStep1: Enter the website URL you want to analyze.

secHeaders.helpStep3: Review the security score, issues list, and improvement recommendations.
secHeaders.helpTip1: Grade A is best, F is worst. Aim for at least grade B.
secHeaders.helpTip2: CSP and HSTS are the two most important security headers.

help.title: SSL/TLS Certificate Checker - User Manual
help.whatIsSslDesc: SSL/TLS is a security protocol that encrypts communication between clients and servers. It ensures data confidentiality and integrity during transmission, and verifies server identity through digital certificates.
help.step1: Single Check: Enter a host address (e.g., example.com) in the input box, set the port number (default 443), and click 'Check SSL/TLS'.
help.step2: Batch Check: Switch to the batch check tab, enter multiple host addresses (one per line), and click 'Check All'.
help.step3: View check results including grade, protocol version, cipher suite, and certificate details.
help.step4: Click the History tab to view previous check results.
help.gradeA: Excellent - Strong protocol, strong cipher, valid certificate
help.gradeB: Good - Minor issues, such as slightly outdated cipher
help.gradeC: Fair - Moderate issues, such as TLS 1.0/1.1 or weak cipher
help.gradeD: Poor - Significant issues, such as expired certificate or very weak cipher
help.gradeF: Fail - Critical issues, such as completely insecure protocol or configuration
help.checkCipher: Cipher suite strength and key exchange

resultFeatures.certificate: Certificate Info: Includes subject, issuer, validity period, SAN domains, etc.

help.title: WAF Detector Help
help.whatIsWafDesc: A Web Application Firewall (WAF) is a security solution that monitors, filters, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web application. It protects against attacks like SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF.
help.methodPayload: Attack payload testing (SQL injection, XSS, etc.)
help.tip1: A high confidence score (>80%) strongly indicates WAF presence.

help.title: Network Discovery - User Manual
help.whatIsNetworkDiscoveryDesc: Network Discovery scans for active hosts and devices within a local network, identifies open ports, running services, operating systems, and presents the connection relationships between devices in a topology diagram.
help.step1: Enter the network range in CIDR format (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) in the scan configuration, and set timeout and concurrency parameters.
help.step2: Select the scan type (TCP/SYN/UDP), and check whether to detect OS and services.
help.step3: Click the 'Start Discovery' button to execute the scan, then view the results and topology preview.
help.step4: Switch to the 'Topology' tab to view the full network topology diagram, and click nodes for host details.
help.feature1: Host Discovery: Discover active hosts in the LAN through ARP tables and port scanning
help.feature2: Port Scanning: Detect open TCP/UDP ports and running services on target hosts
help.feature3: Topology Visualization: Display Internet→Gateway→Host/Device connections using SVG topology diagrams
help.feature4: Security Assessment: Automatically detect high-risk ports and configuration issues, provide security recommendations
help.feature5: Device Classification: Automatically identify device types (routers, servers, desktops, printers, IoT, etc.)
help.topology1: Blue nodes represent the Internet entry point, purple nodes represent gateways/routers
help.topology2: Green nodes represent LAN hosts/devices, purple dashed lines represent DNS connections
help.topology3: Red/yellow dots in the upper right corner of nodes indicate high/medium security risks
help.warning1: Only use for authorized network auditing and security assessments
help.warning2: Scanning may generate load on the target network; it is recommended to run during off-peak hours
help.warning3: Some results may be affected by firewalls and network security policies
